questions.q: What is the mathematical formula used to calculate the speed of a moving object?
questions.a: The formula is Speed = Distance / Time. A student who answers "Distance times Time" or "Time divided by Distance" misunderstands that speed is a rate of change over time, not a total accumulation.

questions.q: If a car travels 100 km in 2 hours, does it mean the car was moving at exactly 50 km/h the entire time?
questions.a: No, it means the *average* speed is 50 km/h. A student who says "Yes" assumes that motion is always uniform, failing to realize that the car might have sped up or slowed down during the journey.

questions.q: A cyclist travels 40 km in 4 hours. What is the speed of the cyclist?
questions.a: The speed is 40 / 4 = 10 km/h. A student who gets this wrong likely divided the time by the distance (4 / 40 = 0.1), showing a confusion between the numerator and denominator in the formula.

questions.q: Why is speed described as a positive number without direction?
questions.a: Speed only measures "how fast," not "where to." A wrong answer suggests the student is confusing speed with velocity, which explicitly requires a specific direction (like "North" or "towards home").

questions.q: If one object moves at 10 m/s and another moves at 10 km/h, which one is faster?
questions.a: The one moving at 10 m/s is faster because 10 m/s is 36 km/h. A wrong answer shows the student is comparing the numbers (10 vs 10) without considering the importance of units.

questions.q: Create a scenario where knowing the speed of an object helps you predict when it will arrive at a specific destination.
questions.a: A student should describe a trip, such as: "If a bus travels at 60 km/h and the town is 120 km away, I know it will take 2 hours to arrive." A poor answer lacks either the distance or the speed component needed to make the prediction.

questions.q: Fill in the blank: Speed is a measure of how fast an object changes its position, ______ by dividing the total distance travelled by the time taken to cover that distance.
Fill in the blank: Imagine you and your ______ are both running to the school gate.
What is Speed? State the definition given in this lesson.
questions.a: Speed is a measure of how fast an object changes its position, calculated by dividing the total distance travelled by the time taken to cover that distance.

questions.q: What common mix-up does this lesson flag about Speed?
questions.a: Students often confuse the units of speed (km/h vs m/s) and treat them as interchangeable without conversion.

questions.q: What must you be able to do to master this topic?
questions.a: The student must be able to calculate speed given distance and time, and identify the correct SI units for these measurements.
